text:
jordan: Heads-up — WavePay (customer id: wp-482) reporting repeated 429s from EU region starting ~2026-02-12 18:02 UTC. Multiple users, high churn. Opening here to triage.

lina: Thanks — any sample request IDs / headers from their client? Can you paste a brief repro or logs?

jordan: Pasted what they sent: `trace=tr-9f3b; status=429; route=/v1/chat/stream; region=eu-west` Also customer shared this header snapshot:```X-RPM-Limit: 1200
X-RPM-Remaining: 0
X-TPM-Limit: 20000
X-TPM-Remaining: 102````

sam: Looks like they exhausted the per-minute bucket (RPM). Remaining=0 is the smoking gun. Are they sending many short streaming sessions or a batch fanout?

jordan: WavePay says they run a bursty reconciliation job every minute that fanouts 60 parallel streams for 20 tenants. They thought tokens were pooled.

lina: Oof. Likely they're exceeding per-second concurrency or per-minute. Two quick checks: 1) ask them to include `X-Request-ID` or `x-trace-id` in failing requests and share one. 2) repro locally with a scaled-down curl script to see rate headers.

sam: Sharing quick curl snippet they can run to reproduce minimal load (1 thread, 10 sec):
```bash
for i in {1..5}; do 
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" 
       -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
       -d '{"model":"rwd-1-small","input":"hi"}' 
       https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate &
done; wait
```
This will surface the `X-RPM-Remaining` header.

jordan: Customer ran that and attached headers. When parallel=60 they see Remaining drop to 0 in ~30s and then 429s for ~20s.

maya: Quick operational context: we enforce two distinct quotas — a rate (RPM) window and a token (TPM) window. The per-tenant minute window is enforced at the edge proxy and backed by a distributed leaky-bucket. Short bursts can blow out the RPM even when TPM still has headroom.

lina: Advice to WavePay: spread your job across sliding windows (stagger start times across seconds) and reduce parallel streams. Also implement exponential backoff + jitter on 429s. Suggest changing 60 parallel -> 6 parallel with a 500ms jitter.

sam: Also possible mitigation on our side: we can bump their RPM for a short window or enable burst-bucket for this tenant if they have a committed plan. @opsbot can you check their plan and commit status?

opsbot: [bot] Tenant wp-482 has standard usage plan (no reserved commit). No current Dedicated capacity. No auto-burst enabled.

jordan: Ok. I'll propose two things to customer: 1) quick client changes (stagger + backoff) for immediate relief, 2) discuss reserved capacity / burst add-on for sustained workloads.

maya: For internal follow-up — we should examine edge proxy metrics at 18:02–18:08 UTC for rpms per-tenant and any hotspotting. If we see cross-tenant interference we may need a short config tweak to token bucket refill alignment.

lina: Can someone grab `edge-proxy` logs for tenant wp-482 for that time window and post a handful of request IDs? I can correlate with rate limiter logs.

sam: I'm on it — pulling logs now. sample request id: `tr-9f3b` shows rule-match: `leaky_bucket_minute` -> dropped at 18:02:37. Full log snippet:
```
[2026-02-12T18:02:37Z] tenant=wp-482 req=tr-9f3b route=/v1/generate status=429 reason=rate_limit bucket=minute limit=1200 remaining=0
```

jordan: Forwarding this to WavePay with recommended client diff and ask to re-run the reduced-parallel test.

maya: Postmortem note: add a short KB entry for 'cron-fanout' customers covering patterns that hit RPM but not TPM. Put in product docs: 'minute-bucket vs token-cost gotchas' and a sample jittered worker pattern.

lina: Agreed. Action items:
- jordan: share guidance + sample script to WavePay (ETA: 30m)
- sam: attach proxy logs and correlate 3 request ids (ETA: 15m)
- maya: draft KB entry and link to docs (ETA: EOD)

jordan: I'm pinging WavePay with that plan. Will update here after they test the 6-parallel variant. :thumbsup:
